paths.name: The first ten
paths.desc: The criteria decided in your design file. Start here.

paths.name: Forms
paths.desc: Labels, errors, sign-in and not asking twice.

paths.name: Motion and time
paths.desc: Animation, flashing, auto-play and time limits.

paths.name: Reviewing work
paths.desc: What to look for in someone else’s flow.

paths.name: Design systems
paths.desc: Rules to build into tokens and components once.

scenarios.text: Form errors are shown only by turning the field’s border red.
scenarios.why: Color is the only cue. Add an error message and an icon — which also satisfies 3.3.1.

scenarios.text: Caption text is #AAAAAA on a white card.
scenarios.why: #AAAAAA on white is about 2.3:1. Text at that size needs 4.5:1.

scenarios.text: A 16×16 close icon sits right against a 16×16 share icon.
scenarios.why: Both are under 24px and too close together for the spacing exception.

scenarios.text: A sign-up form’s only labels are placeholders that vanish as you type.
scenarios.why: Once typing starts, nothing tells people what the field is for. Keep a visible label.

scenarios.text: The focus outline was removed because it “looked messy”.
scenarios.why: Keyboard users lose their place entirely. Design a focus style that fits the brand instead.

scenarios.text: A promo banner image contains the sale price, with no text alternative.
scenarios.why: Meaningful images need a text alternative. Baking text into the image also runs into 1.4.5.

scenarios.text: Pages zoom and slide dramatically as you scroll, and there’s no way to turn it off.
scenarios.why: Interaction-triggered motion must be possible to disable. 2.3.1 is about flashing, not movement.

scenarios.text: Logging in means solving a puzzle, and password managers can’t paste into the field.
scenarios.why: New in WCAG 2.2: no cognitive tests to log in unless there’s an alternative such as paste, passkeys or a magic link.

roles.desc: I design screens and components from a brief.
I own features end to end and hand them to developers.
I shape whole flows and review other designers’ work.
I set standards, systems and priorities for a team.

levelBlurbs.New: You are building the foundations. Lessons start with what each rule is and who it helps.
levelBlurbs.Working: You know the common rules. Lessons start with how to apply and specify them.
levelBlurbs.Fluent: You can cite criteria. Lessons start with trade-offs, reviews and systems.

diagnostic.question: Pale gray text on a white card is hard to read. Which principle does that touch?
Which WCAG level do most laws and policies point to?
What is the minimum contrast for 16px regular body text?
A text field is shown only by its border. What contrast does that border need against the background?
While tabbing, a sticky footer completely covers the focused button. Which criterion fails?
A price slider can only be moved by dragging. What does WCAG 2.2 AA ask for?
options: A way to do it with single taps or clicks

Junior.name: Fix the screen
Junior.desc: One screen, one problem. Pick the fix you would make in the file.

questions.text: A primary button has white text on #6FB1FF. The ratio is about 2.2:1.
options: Darken the blue until white text reaches 4.5:1
Add a soft shadow behind the text
questions.why: Bold 16px still is not large text, and a shadow does not change the ratio. Fix the color pair.

questions.text: A toolbar has 16px icons sitting 4px apart.
options: Keep the glyphs, pad each hit area to 24px or more
questions.why: The glyph can stay small. The area that responds to a tap is what needs room.

questions.text: An invalid field is shown only by a red border.
options: Add an icon and a message that says what is wrong
questions.why: The cue cannot depend on color. Words also tell people how to fix it.

Mid.name: Annotate the handoff
Mid.desc: The design is done. Decide what the developer needs written down.

questions.text: A card has a photo, a title and a “Read more” link. What do you note for the photo?
options: Whether it is decorative or meaningful, and its text alternative
Nothing. Alt text is a developer decision
questions.why: Only the person who chose the image knows what it is there to say.

questions.text: A button opens a modal. Which note prevents the most common bug?
options: Focus moves into the modal, stays there, and returns to the button on close
questions.why: Without it, keyboard focus stays on the page behind the modal.

questions.text: Your layout reads in a different order than a developer would guess from the columns.
options: Number the reading and focus order on the frame
questions.why: Screen readers follow code order. If you do not specify it, it is guessed.

Senior.name: Critique the flow
Senior.desc: You are reviewing a teammate’s work. Choose what matters most.

questions.text: A checkout review finds three issues and there is one sprint. Which goes first?
options: The Pay button cannot be reached by keyboard
The promo carousel has no pause control
questions.why: A total block on the critical path outranks friction. Some people cannot pay at all.

questions.text: The flow asks for the address at shipping, then again at billing.
options: Fine, as long as both are labelled
Offer “same as shipping” or pre-fill it
questions.why: New in 2.2: do not make people re-enter what they already gave in the same process.

questions.text: A designer says the 20-minute session timeout is a security requirement.
options: Ask for a warning before it expires, with a way to extend
Ask for a shorter timeout so it is noticed
questions.why: The limit can stay. People need to be warned and able to extend it.

Lead.name: Make the call
Lead.desc: No single screen to fix. Decide the rule, the priority, the argument.

questions.text: Brand wants white text on the primary yellow, #FFB400. It measures about 1.8:1.
options: Keep the yellow, pair it with dark text, and ship the pair as a token
questions.why: 1.8:1 fails even for large text. The hue can stay. The pairing changes, once, for everyone.

questions.text: Where does a contrast rule do the most good?
options: In tokens and components every team inherits
questions.why: Audits find problems after they are built. Systems stop them being built.

questions.text: A stakeholder says accessibility can wait until after launch.
options: Show the cost of retrofitting and scope the AA essentials into this release
Say it is the right thing to do
Agree and add it to the backlog
questions.why: Values rarely move a roadmap. Cost, risk and a small, concrete scope do.

laws.note: Covers many consumer products and services. Its technical standard, EN 301 549, builds on WCAG Level AA.
Section 508 covers federal agencies. ADA rules for state and local government name WCAG Level AA.
Public sector websites and apps are expected to meet WCAG Level AA.

laws.law: Accessible Canada Act, AODA in Ontario
laws.note: Federal and provincial rules that reference WCAG.
Official guidance uses WCAG as the reference.
